title.en: Explain the role of the public sector in development
Describe the changes in government policy since 1991

say.en: After independence, the government built steel plants, dams and power stations because private firms lacked the money and the will. Since 1991 its role has changed: it now invites private investment and sells part of its shares. In this lesson: Explain the role of the public sector in development.
Describe the changes in government policy since 1991.

body.en: The *public sector* built infrastructure such as power, transport and heavy industry that private firms could not finance. It promoted balanced regional development by setting up units in backward areas, achieved economies of scale, checked the concentration of economic power, and helped import substitution by making at home what was earlier imported.

title.en: On the board: Changing role of the public sector

narration.en: After independence the public sector was given five big jobs.

say.en: After independence the public sector was given five big jobs.
In 1991 the new industrial policy changed this role. Industries reserved for the public sector fell from seventeen to eight.
Four changes came in 1991: fewer reserved industries, disinvestment, review of sick units, and MoUs for autonomy.
Disinvestment means selling government shares to the public. Sell 26 per cent of a fully owned company and the government still holds 74.
But if more than 49 per cent is sold, government holding falls below 51 and it is no longer a government company.

problem.en: The government owns 100% of a public enterprise with 50 crore shares. It sells 12 crore shares to the public through disinvestment. What percentage does it still own, and is the enterprise still a government company?

steps.en: Shares left with the government = 50 − 12 = 38 crore.
76% is at least 51%, so it remains a government company.

narration.en: Let us work through this case together. The government owns 100% of a public enterprise with 50 crore shares. It sells 12 crore shares to the public through disinvestment. What percentage does it still own, and is the enterprise still a government company?

say.en: Let us work through this case together. The government owns 100 percent of a public enterprise with 50 crore shares. It sells 12 crore shares to the public through disinvestment. What percentage does it still own, and is the enterprise still a government company?
Shares left with the government equals 50 minus 12 equals 38 crore.
Holding equals 38 divided by 50 times 100 equals 76 percent.
76 percent is at least 51 percent, so it remains a government company.
So the answer is 76 percent; yes, still a government company.
